summary: Masao Shizutani worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and history and archaeology. He held posts as assistant professor at Josai University and at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, attested in 1974.

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy, Masaru Akimoto served at Kyoto Women's University, where he is attested as a professor in the Faculty of Contemporary Society in 2002 and again attested in 2015.

Masashi Nagai specialized in Buddhist studies, earning his degrees at Komazawa University. He served as lecturer (1984), assistant professor (1988, 1994), professor emeritus (2017), and president (2019) at Komazawa University, and also held posts at Soto Zen Research Center and the Museum of Zen Culture and History.

Masataka Suzuki specializes in religious studies, history and archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Keio University (~1969–1978) and taught there (~1989–2015), later serving as a lecturer at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies, attested in 2026.

Masataro Sawayanagi studied at the University of Tokyo (~1885–1888). He later held posts at Tohoku University (~1911–1913), Kyushu University (~1913–1914), Tokyo University of Education, and Taisho University (~1926–1927).

Masato Kobayashi works in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1989–1995) and completed his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania (~1995–2000) under George Cardona, later serving as a research fellow at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~2000–2002).

Masatoshi Konishi worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied at International Christian University, University of Calcutta, University of Tokyo, and Rikkyo University. He was an assistant professor at Hosei University (1971–1984) and professor emeritus at Rikkyo University (1984–2003).

Masatoshi Nagatomi worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku University, Kyoto University, and Harvard University under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, becoming an instructor of Sanskrit at Harvard in 1958.

Masayuki Taira is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and Japanology who studied at Kyoto University (~1970–1978). He held positions at Kansai University (~1982–1987), Osaka University (~1987–2017), and Kyoto Tachibana University (~2017).

Masayuki Tsukimoto works in Japanology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. In 2026, he is attested as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Massimo Pallottino was an archaeologist and historian who studied at the Sapienza University of Rome (~1927–1931). He held positions at the University of Cagliari (~1940–1945) and the Sapienza University of Rome (~1945–1980).

Masumi Mochizuki specializes in Buddhist studies. His career includes appointments at Minobusan University as a lecturer in the Faculty of Buddhist Studies (attested 2001), professor (attested 2015), and special appointment professor (attested 2026).
Mathew Varghese works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He served as a research fellow (2012) and lecturer (attested 2026) at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

Mathieu Beaudouin specializes in linguistics, Tibetology, and Sinology, earning degrees from Panthéon-Sorbonne University and INALCO. He has taught at INALCO, Sorbonne Nouvelle, Hamilton College, and EPHE, becoming a British Academy International Fellow at the University of Cambridge in 2025.

Mathieu Boisvert works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Anthony Kennedy Warder and Ravindra Panth. He founded and, beginning in 1992, served as a professor at the Université du Québec à Montréal.
Mathilde Deromps was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Jules Bloch from 1911 to 1914.

Mathurin Veyssière de La Croze worked in linguistics, history and archaeology, and Indology. He served as a librarian at Humboldt University of Berlin (1697) and as librarian and antiquary at the Royal Library of Berlin (~1697–1739).

Matteo Bartoli was a linguist who studied at the universities of Vienna, Strasbourg, and Paris under Michele Kerbaker and Heinrich Hübschmann. He held posts at the University of Pisa (1907–1908) and the University of Turin (1908–1946).

Matthew Atmore Sherring studied at University College London (1848–1850) and Coward College (~1848–1851), working in Indology and religious studies. In 1852, he took a post as a missionary with the London Missionary Society.

Matthew B. Orsborn completed his PhD at the University of Hong Kong (–2012) under Guang Xing and Yakupitiyage Karunadasa, also studying under Hsing Yun and Huishang. In 2026, he is attested as professor and Head of the International Affairs Section at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies.
